inventory_summary: src/i-state-access.hpp: no asserts or throws. WARL legalization is applied on read and on write for every WARL CSR, the same way for direct (do_read_*) and shadow-preferring (uarch bridge) accessors. Values come from the hashed shadow registers, which the guest changes only through instruction semantics.

src/state-access.hpp (native): assert(i != 0) in do_write_x (the interpreter never writes x0). do_read_memory/do_write_memory catch every exception and return false; only virtio, which reproducible machines refuse, reaches them. The throws in do_write_memory_with_padding (data null, write_length < data_length) are unreachable from send_cmio_response: machine::send_cmio_response refuses a null buffer when length <= rx length, and an oversized response is a no-op before any write. do_read_pma relies on machine_address_ranges::read_pma, which returns a sentinel for an out-of-range index. poll_external_interrupts and getchar act only for unreproducible machines (R1-R2-1 and R3-VARSHADOW-1 families, not re-reported).

src/record-send-cmio-state-access.hpp (honest log producer): the alignment and nullptr throws are unreachable with the honest arguments. update_after_write drops update_hash_tree_page's result in NDEBUG, but hash_tree::update_page only returns true or throws, so nothing is lost. log_write_memory_with_padding writes the revert root hash through machine::write_memory's special case (0xfe0, 32 bytes) and writes the rx buffer, which is never host-read-only. The log is self-verified by replay_send_cmio_state_access. I compared check_read/check_write/check_write_memory_with_padding against what the recorder emits, field by field (sizes, read/written data, written hash, address, log2 size): honest logs always pass.

send-cmio-response.cpp through the state accessors: dataLength is a uint32 that the input sender chooses. uint32Log2 and uint32ShiftLeft never shift by 32. Every length above 2^21 is a no-op. imcyclemax saturates. Sizes the input sender controls bound no allocation (the replay calloc is at most 2 MiB).

src/uarch-record-state-access.hpp (honest log producer): the 'error updating hash tree' throws are unreachable (update_page throws or returns true). machine::write_word/write_reg refusals (x0, uarch_x0, marchid, mvendorid, mimpid, protected/read-only/device ranges, shadow gaps) are reachable only by a uarch store that the pristine uarch program never issues (R1-R10-1 family). adjust_access logs the unaligned address for a misaligned access, but uarch-step's require() refuses misaligned accesses first. The record and replay paths agree on every access kind: word read/write, register read/write, TLB slot write, uarch reset (pristine hash), and revert root hash read. log_reset_uarch's comparison against context.root_hash_after covers both the reverting and the non-reverting reset.

src/uarch-replay-state-access.hpp (support, but on the honest path through log_step_uarch/log_reset_uarch self-verification): make_proof checks sibling count and read/written sizes before any data is used, so get_word_access_data's assert cannot fire. For each check I confirmed that an honestly recorded access passes, so the self-verification never rejects an honest log.

src/collect-mcycle-hashes-state-access.hpp: the dirty-page invariant ('only mcycle writes mark registers') holds. interpret_loop writes mcycle on every non-throwing exit, and write_iflags_X(0) and device register writes happen inside a run that ends in that write. Memory writes (stores, AMOs, PTE A/D updates through write_ram_uint64) all go through do_write_memory_word, which marks the page. TLB writes mark the slot page. do_read_memory/do_write_memory throw only through virtio. assert(index < PMA_MAX) has a safe release fallback (sentinel).

src/collect-uarch-cycle-hashes-state-access.hpp: every uarch write path marks the dirty word (write_word, shadow uarch registers, all three TLB slot fields, which lie in one 32-byte word). The direct reset (uarch_registers_state{} plus a memcpy of only the dirtied uarch RAM words) matches machine::reset_uarch, because UARCH_*_INIT equal the struct defaults and the call checks the uarch state is pristine on entry. reset_uarch throws only if called, and the collector never calls it.

uarch/uarch-bridge-state-access.hpp (compiled into the uarch with asserts on): the do_read_memory/do_write_memory aborts are unreachable (only virtio uses them). The mock address range aborts need a PMA table that disagrees with its own decoding. The table is guest-read-only and host-write-protected, and loading memcmp-checks it, so only an invalid template reaches them. An out-of-range pma_index returns the sentinel, as native read_pma does. interpret_next_mcycle_with_uarch's mcycle+1 wraps only at mcycle 2^64-1, which is already the overflow fixed point.

src/shadow-tlb.hpp, shadow-registers.hpp, shadow-uarch-state.hpp, machine-reg.hpp: the address/what mapping functions refuse misaligned and out-of-range addresses (unknown_). TLB_INVALID_PAGE and TLB_UNVERIFIED_PAGE are never page-aligned, so no guest vaddr_page collides with them. shadow_tlb_verify_slot is shared by native init_hot_tlb_slot, uarch verify_cold_tlb_slot and mark_write_tlb_dirty_page, so the 'TLB is corrupt' throw cannot fire on a slot that passed verification.

src/access-log.hpp and its JSON decoding (json-util.cpp access/access_log): log2_size is bounded to INT_MAX and then validated by make_proof. The sibling vector and data are bounded by the input size. Bracket 'where' is range-checked. No allocation is sized by an unchecked field. (The JSON hash_tree_proof decoder allocates root-target siblings before validating, up to 64 GiB for log2_root_size=INT_MAX, but its only caller is the JSON-RPC client parsing replies from its trusted server, so I did not report it.)
not_covered: record-step-state-access.hpp / replay-step-state-access.hpp (main-processor step logs): skipped as ZK-only and out of scope.

hash_tree internals reached from the state accessors (update_page, update_words, page_hash_tree_cache borrow/return, enqueue_hash_entry): I read only the parts the accessors depend on. I did not check page-cache staleness between update_page (borrow without the dense-hash check) and update_words, and I did not fault-inject.
No dynamic or differential experiments were run in this round. Every conclusion comes from reading the code side by side (native vs record vs replay vs collectors vs uarch bridge).
uarch-solidity-compat.hpp helpers other than the state wrappers, and the generated Solidity counterparts of the state accessors (EmulatorCompat.sol / AccessLogs.sol), which earlier rounds covered.
Worst-case uarch cycle count per mcycle against UARCH_CYCLE_MAX (collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes throws on overflow): not re-measured. I relied on the earlier R1-R12-2 analysis.
Lua-side conversion of access logs (cartesi Lua module to JSON to C++), and the JSON-RPC server's decoding of log_* / verify_* requests beyond the json-util functions named above.
i-device-state-access / device-state-access paths of the CLINT, PLIC and HTIF devices themselves: I checked only that their register writes are covered by the collectors' dirty tracking.
